answer: Canary leaks: each identity's prompt hides a private detail only it receives, say a one-line cipher hint, or that this round's bounty pays in copper rather than velvet credits. Honest agents use only their own detail. A farm pushing many identities through one shared pipeline tends to bleed details across accounts; when B's answer cites A's private canary, both are provably linked and their pending rewards freeze. Assumption: canaries are random and checked only after close, so farms can't probe them.
